title: An import row with the number of a part stocked here updates that part
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create a part, part A, for this test at the test location, with Min 1 and Max 5.
  • Have a parts import file with one row for part A, with part A's exact part number, its description, Min 2 and Max 6.
  • Start on the Inventory data import page (Settings, then Data Import, then Inventory).
custom_steps:
1. Upload the file.
  2. Run the import.
  3. Click Parts in the top bar.
  4. Click Inventory in the left menu.
  5. Type part A's part number in the Search box.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The file is ready to import.

Step 2:

  • The import finishes without refusing the row: no "already exists at this location" message appears.

Step 3:

  • The Parts left menu shows Inventory.

Step 4:

  • The Inventory page opens.

Step 5:

  • One row is listed for part A, now with Min 2 and Max 6 (it had 1 and 5): the row updated the part already stocked here.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10820 (Story 7, Create a Part by Typing Its Number and Description), story SV-10826 (Story 13, The Part Dialog)

  • S7-N7: “S7-N3 to S7-N6 do not apply to the parts CSV import. An import row whose number matches a part already stocked at this location updates that part (S13-N9a). It is never refused for a duplicate number.”
  • S13-N9a: “When an import row's number matches a Part Library entry that is already stocked as a part at this location, the import updates that part. It never adds a second part on the same entry. A match ignores upper and lower case, hyphens, asterisks, periods and spaces, so re-importing an old number that differs from the new one only in those ways updates the renamed part.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
